Support Life Cycle Policy

Check Point’s Enterprise Support Lifecycle policies outline the product support guidelines for a product’s lifecycle. The objective of this policy is to standardize and normalize product lifecycle practices to assist you in making an informed purchase, and support and upgrade decisions. All Check Point products (except third-party products sold by Check Point) are covered by this policy. Customers who are operating Check Point products under a valid Support & Maintenance Agreement are entitled to the benefits associated with this policy.

Software Support

Software Support Lifecycle Policy Guidelines

Check Point is committed to providing support for all software products for a minimum of four years, starting from the general availability date. ‘General Availability date’ is defined as the date on which a product is officially made available for purchase. In addition, Check Point aims to support a minimum of two versions of all software products. Check Point usually ends support for a software release only when:

  • Four years have elapsed since the release of the version in question
  • The above is relevant to the following product categories listed below: (a) Security Gateway and Management; (b) Check Point Spark Firewall Security Gateways; (c) Check Point Maestro Hyperscale Firewall; (d) Endpoint Security and Remote Access up to Jun 1, 2022
  • As for Endpoint Security and Remote Access as of Jun 1, 2022, Check Point is committed to providing support for all software products for a period of at least 18 months starting from the general availability date. ‘General Availability date’ is defined as the date on which a product is officially made available for purchase. In addition, for endpoint security and remote access, Check Point will support once a year, one of the versions for an extended period of 30 months as of the GA date.

Endpoint Security for Linux

Each major release of CPLA is supported for one year.
This support does not include issues caused by upgrades to the Linux distribution. Such issues will be addressed in either:

  • a new major release, or
  • a minor release of the latest major version.

Current release version numbering:

In the 1.X.y, 1.X is the major version and .y is the minor one.

For example, in 1.28.12, 1.28 is the major version and .12 is the minor one.

From version 2 and above:

In the A.b.c, A is the major version and .b.c is the minor one.

For example, in 2.1.3, 2 is the major version and .1.3 is the minor one.

Appliances Support

Appliance Support Lifecycle Policy Guidelines

Check Point provides a comprehensive support lifecycle for its appliances, including Software and Operating System support.

Software and Operating Systems

  • The appliance software release is supported according to the software life cycle policy. In case no supported software releases are compatible with the appliance model, the latest compatible version will be supported until the appliance end of support date.
  • Engineering Support: Maintenance releases are supplied until 3 three years after End of Sale Date
  • End of support: Software upgrades and bug fixes will be supplied until 5 five years after End of Sale Date to handle support issues. New software releases may require the purchase of hardware upgrades by the customer

Technical Assistance

  • Full TAC support from the Check Point Technical Assistance centers is supplied until 5 five years after End of Sale Date.

Hardware

  • Units and parts can be replaced via Check Point’s RMA process. Check Point will provide same or similar parts or full unit replacement when needed.
  • End of support: RMA process will be available until 5 five years after End of Sale Date or until the official End of Support Date Announcement (whichever is earlier).
